Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}3y=-x \\ 2y=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}x+3y=0 \\ 2y=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 2-0\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
